communication_expectations: Carly is a 38-year-old physical therapist. Clear, adult, professional communication is expected; she values open, empathetic discussion and being involved in decisions. She understands medical terminology, so precise language is acceptable, but empathy must not be replaced by clinical talk.
caregiver_rules: Not applicable - Carly speaks for herself.
patient_goals: Return to cycling, kickboxing, and HIIT workouts
Be able to take good care of her son Finn

assessment_areas.case_context: Bilateral wrist pain (4-5/10) that began with a heavier manual-therapy caseload, with numbness/tingling in a median-nerve-like distribution. Symptom behavior (aggravating/easing activities, timing, sensory changes) should be characterized.
acceptable_approaches: open questions about what makes symptoms better or worse
function-first questions (gripping, lifting, patient care)
following up on numbness or tingling disclosures

assessment_areas.case_context: She works part-time as a PT with a manual-therapy-heavy caseload; her symptoms threaten her professional confidence and ergonomics are hard to control.
acceptable_approaches: exploring what her workday involves
exploring how symptoms affect patient care
exploring her concerns about continuing manual therapy

assessment_areas.case_context: Breast cancer diagnosed 3 weeks ago; radiation, chemotherapy, and total mastectomy are planned. This is emotionally sensitive and should be approached with permission-seeking and empathy, not interrogation.
acceptable_approaches: open, gentle exploration of how she is doing with the diagnosis
asking what treatment is planned and what support she has
following her lead on depth

assessment_areas.case_context: Her son Finnegan has cerebral palsy (reverse rolling walker, communication difficulty); she worries about her husband Drew coping while she undergoes treatment.
acceptable_approaches: asking about home responsibilities and support
responding to disclosures about Finn or Drew with follow-up

assessment_areas.case_context: Her confidence is shaken; the family is under significant emotional strain. Emotional cues should be acknowledged and explored.
acceptable_approaches: reflective responses to emotional cues
direct but kind questions about coping and support

assessment_areas.case_context: Mother, aunt, and paternal grandmother had breast cancer in their 40s - relevant context she can share if asked.
acceptable_approaches: standard family-history questions

assessment_areas.case_context: She wakes more often overnight since her condition began and daytime sleepiness sometimes interferes with her day.
acceptable_approaches: screening sleep quality and changes

assessment_areas.case_context: She exercises about 3 days/week (cycling, kickboxing, HIIT) and exercise is her stress outlet; wrist pain is limiting some activities.
acceptable_approaches: asking what she enjoys and what has changed
connecting exercise to her goals and coping

assessment_areas.case_context: With progressive numbness/tingling and an active cancer diagnosis, appropriate screening includes symptom progression, night symptoms, and general health changes - without alarming or diagnosing.
acceptable_approaches: asking whether sensory symptoms are changing or waking her
asking about general health changes since diagnosis
screening woven into symptom exploration

assessment_areas.assessment_area: pediatric/school topics directed at the patient
assessment_areas.case_context: School-style pediatric questioning is not applicable to Carly herself.
